title: Truncated Polyakov bootstrap for BCFTs: Neumann-Dirichlet flow and Ising special transition
authors: Kaushik Kangsabanik, Apratim Kaviraj, Astha Tiwari
abstract: We extend the recently proposed truncated Polyakov bootstrap to boundary conformal field theories (BCFTs). The formalism uses the analytic functional framework to find approximate solutions of BCFT crossing. We show that a generic nonperturbative solution can be identified by relating it to a family of deformations around generalized free fields (GFF) with a fixed boundary condition. We show this by tracking the flow of BCFT data from GFF with Neumann boundary condition to that with Dirichlet. The same method is then used for the 3d Ising special transition, using the perturbative Wilson-Fisher description as the deformation to identify it. The BCFT data obtained are in remarkable agreement with existing lattice results where available, and are otherwise new.
summary: This work extends the Polyakov bootstrap technique to Boundary Conformal Field Theories (BCFTs) to solve for crossing equations. By analyzing the flow between Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and by applying the method to the 3D Ising special transition, the authors derive new, consistent predictions for critical exponents that match existing lattice data.
main_problem: The paper extends the truncated Polyakov bootstrap formalism to Boundary Conformal Field Theories (BCFTs) to find approximate solutions for BCFT crossing equations.
main_result: The formalism successfully relates the flow of BCFT data between different boundary conditions (Neumann to Dirichlet) and provides a bootstrap for the 3D Ising special transition, showing agreement with lattice results.
method: It uses the analytic functional framework and the truncated Polyakov bootstrap by minimizing a loss function derived from functional sum rules to determine unknown BCFT parameters.
model_or_system: The study focuses on BCFTs, which describe critical phenomena near a boundary. Specific applications include the flow between Generalized Free Fields (GFF) with Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and the 3D Ising special transition.
key_observables: Boundary operator dimensions ($\hat{\Delta}_n$), bulk OPE coefficients ($\mu^2_{\Delta n}$), and the structure of the 2-point function decomposed into bulk and boundary conformal blocks.
important_parameters: The flow parameter $\epsilon$ (used to connect dimensions from free theory to the 3D Ising limit, $\epsilon=1$), and deformation parameters ($\gamma_n, \delta_n, ho_n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of a functional basis for correlators exhibiting the boundedness property, and the use of a 'truncated' bootstrap due to the crossing equation not being positive semi-definite.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the flow of boundary operator dimensions ($\hat{\Delta}_n$), OPE coefficients ($\mu^2_{\Delta n}$), and other parameters as the boundary condition changes from Neumann to Dirichlet. A final table compiles the calculated boundary spectrum for the 3D Ising case.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the formalism by applying it to the Neumann-to-Dirichlet flow, establishing the method. It then applies this machinery to bootstrap the 3D Ising special transition by performing a dimensional flow analysis using Padé approximants to connect the free theory limit ($\epsilon 	o 0$) to the critical point ($\epsilon=1$).
why_interesting: The rigorous application of bootstrap methods to boundary critical phenomena provides powerful, non-perturbative constraints on the spectrum of boundary operators, which is crucial for understanding critical behavior in confined geometries.
